correctness.rationale: For any transformation, sufficiently large common-multiple powers produce a unique eventual idempotent. Power adjacency preserves this idempotent, so its fiber is exactly the graph component. Conditions on root permutation, kernel-fiber images, and acyclicity away from roots are equivalent to lying in a fixed component. The directed matrix-tree determinant for each root permutation is evaluated using Sylvester's lemma and a permutation-cycle product, yielding the exact formula. All n=1..6 transformations and direct \(n\le 5\) graph components independently check out.

originality.rationale: The proof establishes an explicit all-rank component cardinality formula via fiber-preserving permutations and directed-forest determinants. Zeng et al. 2025 give the idempotent component classification and trivial high-rank group cardinalities, but neither their full Section 3 nor Sections 3–4 of Eze et al. 2026 present a profile-dependent exact component-size formula. The 17-versus-11 rank-two split at \(n=5\) lies beyond the previously tabulated \(n\le 4\) graphs. Scientific-index semantic searches of component sizes, eventual idempotents, kernel partitions and rooted forests did not return an implication-equivalent entry; this is bounded evidence, not proof of global novelty.
residual_risks: An older, differently named count of roots of arbitrary idempotents in \(T_{n}\) or a directed-forest assignment formula may imply the same numerical identity even if absent from the inspected power-graph papers.
Neither semantic search nor full inspection of two highly relevant articles proves historical uniqueness across the full semigroup enumeration literature.

value.rationale: This supplies an exact size for every power-graph connected component of the full transformation semigroup for every n, indexed by the natural kernel-fiber profile. It answers an intrinsic quantification absent from the known qualitative component classification, and reveals first nonuniform same-rank component sizes at \(n=5\), namely 17 versus 11. The constrained directed-forest reduction is mathematically structural, and the formula subsumes known \(n\le 4\) and top-rank results without claiming them as new.
